subject: Electrical Engineering
title: PID in the Real World
description: A 60-second lesson on PID in the Real World.

hook.text: Over 90% of industrial controllers use PID. It's the most successful control algorithm ever.

buildup.text: Temperature control in chemical plants: PID adjusts heater power to hold exact temperatures.

discovery.text: Cruise control in cars: PID adjusts throttle to maintain the set speed on varying terrain.

twist.text: Some systems cascade multiple PID loops — an inner loop for fast response, an outer loop for precision.

climax.text: From quadcopter stabilization to steel mill rollers, PID runs the physical world quietly.

punchline.text: Simple, robust, everywhere — PID control is engineering's quiet workhorse.

quiz.question: What is cascade control?
options: Using one PID controller for many different systems simultaneously
Nesting multiple PID loops where the outer loop's output sets the inner loop's setpoint
Running PID at two different clock speeds alternately
